recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If OO wants to re-exclude patient-reported-name from DeviceDefinition, that should be handled by a new work-group decision because later published/applied issues intentionally reshaped the shared DeviceNameType value set and binding.
issue_request: FHIR-23868 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and requested clearer DeviceNameType code definitions, updated Device.deviceName and DeviceDefinition.deviceName definitions, and removal of patient-reported-name from the value set used by DeviceDefinition.deviceName.
initial_application: Commit 439f71f709 listed FHIR-23868 among several Device issues applied to the old spreadsheet source. The reworked XML source in commits such as 33b409a4b6 and c69d71aa21 then contained the seed-era clarified user-friendly-name, patient-reported-name, manufacturer-name, and model-name definitions plus the Device/DeviceDefinition name definition split.
additional_context: Later Published issue FHIR-20639 replaced the seed-era DeviceNameType list with registered-name, user-friendly-name, and patient-reported-name and updated DeviceDefinition.deviceName.type. FHIR-39162 later consolidated Device.deviceName into Device.name, FHIR-43164 made DeviceDefinition.deviceName.type and Device.name.type extensible CodeableConcepts with jurisdictional guidance, and the already-published FHIR-47605 reconciliation added commercial-brand-family to both active bindings. FHIR-55255 is only Resolved - change required context for a future THO move and was not in the default applied/published source-edit scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Device and DeviceDefinition are active resources, their current name definitions preserve the manufacturer/patient distinction, and the current DeviceNameType concepts reflect later approved replacements. Recreating an older DeviceDefinition-only patient-reported-name exclusion would conflict with later decisions that keep a shared, extensible name-type binding.
